articles.title: A Drift Detector That Cries Wolf Is Worse Than No Detector
articles.excerpt: My drift detector quarantined a healthy agent. The agent hadn't gotten worse — the benchmark had gotten bigger. The detector compared failure counts across corpus versions, so growing the benchmark fr…
articles.body: My drift detector quarantined a healthy agent. The agent hadn't gotten worse — the benchmark had gotten bigger. The detector compared failure counts across corpus versions, so growing the benchmark from 10 tasks to 20 made a 10/10 agent look like it "failed" half the suite. Corpus growth looked like decay. I built the drift detector for HivePlane v0.2.0 to catch the failure mode I'd written about in v0.1.0 — "the dangerous agent usually drifted, not got edited." The harder problem turned out not to be detecting drift. It was not detecting drift that wasn't there. A detector that cries wolf trains operators to ignore the signal, and an ignored gate is no gate.
articles.author: Debashish Ghosal

articles.title: taming cold‑start latency in supabase edge functions (typescript)
articles.excerpt: while building a low‑latency analytics dashboard on supabase edge functions, the first request after a few minutes of inactivity consistently hit ~800 ms latency. the spike broke the UI's 200 ms frame…
articles.body: while building a low‑latency analytics dashboard on supabase edge functions, the first request after a few minutes of inactivity consistently hit ~800 ms latency. the spike broke the UI's 200 ms frame budget and forced me to rethink the function deployment. why edge cold‑starts matter edge functions run in lightweight containers that spin down after a period of inactivity. when a new request arrives the platform pulls the latest bundle, resolves dependencies and starts the runtime. this process is fast compared to traditional VMs, but it’s still enough to cause noticeable jitter in real‑time UIs. three pragmatic knobs to pull bundle size – every kilobyte adds network and unzip time. using esbuild with --bundle --minify strips dead code and inlines small assets.

articles.title: Claude in Your Coding Agent: Anthropic's API, Amazon Bedrock, or Any Gateway
articles.excerpt: Claude is the model a lot of teams want for coding, but the way they pay for it differs. Some have an Anthropic API key. Some buy everything through AWS, so Claude reaches them through Amazon Bedrock.…
articles.body: Claude is the model a lot of teams want for coding, but the way they pay for it differs. Some have an Anthropic API key. Some buy everything through AWS, so Claude reaches them through Amazon Bedrock. Some run a company gateway that every request has to pass through. Since Atlarix 15.9, all three work the same way inside the agent, in the desktop app, the CLI, VS Code and the editors that speak the Agent Client Protocol. This is how to connect each one. Why one format covers all three Anthropic publishes its own API, the Messages API : POST /v1/messages , a key, and a version header. Amazon Bedrock offers Claude on an endpoint that speaks the same format, and so do many gateways and proxies. So the question Atlarix asks is not "which company" but "which format".

articles.title: Training a 97.5M Python coding model from scratch for $1.40 in GPU time
articles.excerpt: I wanted to really understand how language models are built, and the best way I know to understand something is to build it. So I built a small one myself, from nothing: my own tokenizer, my own model…
articles.body: I wanted to really understand how language models are built, and the best way I know to understand something is to build it. So I built a small one myself, from nothing: my own tokenizer, my own model, my own training loop, fine-tuning and benchmark. I kept it to Python code only, and kept it small enough that I could afford to train it. The main pre-training run used about $1.40 of rented GPU time. The result Keera solved 9 of 164 HumanEval problems (5.5%) using greedy decoding, after solving 3 (1.8%) before fine-tuning. Pre-training the 97.5M-parameter model took 2 h 23 min on a rented RTX 5090, costing approximately $1.40 in training-time rental charges. These are preliminary results: I haven't checked the training data for overlap with HumanEval.

articles.title: Support Knowledge Freshness: What Scrape Plus Embed Operations Look Like
articles.excerpt: A scrape plus embed pipeline looks healthy only when changed product content becomes searchable on time and the right passage returns within the retrieval latency budget. The page, however, arrives as…
articles.body: A scrape plus embed pipeline looks healthy only when changed product content becomes searchable on time and the right passage returns within the retrieval latency budget. The page, however, arrives as a retrieval-latency SLO burn alert: the on-call sees support searches timing out, a queue of recently changed product pages, and an index that is serving yesterday's material, while restarting workers may shorten the queue without answering the important question of whether the system lost time while fetching, parsing, embedding, publishing, or querying. The page is late.

articles.title: Developer Changelog Retrieval: Tenant Boundaries, Freshness, and Citation Cost
articles.excerpt: Short answer: use a tenant-scoped vector index for durable changelog history, add web retrieval only for pages whose freshness contract demands it, and make the tenant boundary part of every retrieval…
articles.body: Short answer: use a tenant-scoped vector index for durable changelog history, add web retrieval only for pages whose freshness contract demands it, and make the tenant boundary part of every retrieval request and citation. This keeps a fintech changelog tracker from trading a lower index bill for a cross-tenant disclosure or a stale answer. The cost that matters is not the number of vectors by itself. It is the number of vectors you must search, refresh, and explain when a developer asks, “What changed?” A tracker that watches payment-provider release notes has two clocks: the clock of the indexed archive and the clock of the live page. Treating them as one source makes the system hard to reason about.

articles.title: One Misplaced Block Made Every Message Rewrite 19,000 Cached Tokens
articles.excerpt: Prompt caching is the cheapest win in an AI coding agent. The system prompt and tool definitions are the same on every request, so the provider can keep them and charge a fraction for reading them bac…
articles.body: Prompt caching is the cheapest win in an AI coding agent. The system prompt and tool definitions are the same on every request, so the provider can keep them and charge a fraction for reading them back. Atlarix has marked its prompt for caching for a long time, and the logs looked right. Then a QA pass compared two messages in the same chat, byte for byte, and found that in Build mode every message after the first rewrote the whole cache instead of reading it. How the cache works, briefly Claude's cache matches on an exact prefix : tools, then the system prompt, then the conversation, up to a marked breakpoint. If any byte before the breakpoint changes, everything from that byte on is a miss and is written to the cache again.

The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. articles.body: HBO and HBO Max's " Lanterns " served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were. While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling. After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
